terms.def: A special ability every character of one race gets for free, like a Troll's faster attacks.
The hero a player creates and plays: one race (like Undead), one class (like Mage) and a name.
The way a character focuses its class, for example a Mage who studies Frost rather than Fire.
Points a character earns while levelling and spends on upgrades that shape its spec.
A stronger version of the same spell, learned later; Rank 3 hits harder than Rank 1.
The wait before a spell or ability can be used again.
A helpful effect cast on a player that lasts a while, such as more health or more mana.
The player who stands in front and keeps the monsters hitting them instead of the group.
The player who keeps everyone alive by restoring their health.
A player whose job is to defeat the monsters as fast as possible.
A big challenge for 10 to 40 players at once, with the hardest bosses and the best rewards.
A shorter adventure for a group of five players, ending with bosses.
A powerful named monster at the end of a dungeon or raid.
One of 65 account-wide goals, each worth one legacy point, such as reaching level 25 with a class or 150 skill in a crafting profession.
A cloth worn over armor that shows a design.
Account-wide points earned by finishing challenges, spent on rewards for any character.
A paid bundle that includes the game time and extras, and lets its owner reserve names early.
Paid time to play: a monthly subscription or a block of Game Time; the game needs one of them from launch.
Numbers that shape a character: Stamina adds health, Intellect adds mana, Spirit refills health and mana faster.
A big open square inside Orgrimmar, the Horde's main city, where groups often meet.
One of the two sides a player chooses; the five of this board all play Horde.
The other side; Horde and Alliance players cannot group together.
A server type where players only fight each other if they choose to.
Fighting other players instead of computer-controlled monsters.
The highest level a character can reach; in Forever it is 60.
The pool of energy a spellcaster spends to cast spells.
How long a character has to stand still while a spell charges before it goes off.
A stat on gear that makes spells hit harder or heal more.
The small box the game shows when you point at a spell or item, listing what it does.
A craft or gathering skill, such as Tailoring or Mining, that any character can learn.
A copy of the same world zone that the game uses to spread out crowds of players.
Marked this way when Blizzard or the game files say it directly.
The date the facts on a page describe.
The last date someone re-read the sources behind a page.
A version of the game's own files; numbers read from them are what the game ships.
Information dug out of the game files by fans before Blizzard announces it; it can change.
A small change Blizzard makes to the live game without a download.
The official message boards where Blizzard staff post news and answers.
A test server where players can try changes before they go live.
An early test version of the game that some players could play before launch.
A character's job, such as Mage, Priest or Warlock; it sets the spells, the armor and whether it can tank, heal or deal damage. Forever has nine.
A character's people, such as Undead, Troll or Tauren; it sets the look, a few special abilities and which classes are open.
One of the two sides, Horde or Alliance; players of different sides cannot group together, and each race belongs to one side.
A named club of players who chat and play together; in Forever its members need the same ruleset and the same side to group.
A task given by a character in the game, such as defeating monsters or fetching items, that rewards experience; Forever adds over 1,000 new ones.
A creature a character rides to travel faster; riding training comes with a first mount, and Blizzard has not published its price yet.
The game's money, counted in gold, silver and copper; it pays for spells from trainers, riding, repairs and items other players sell.
A monster's attention: it attacks whoever has the most. The tank works to hold it so the monsters hit them, not the rest of the group.
A harmful effect on a player or monster that lasts a while, such as a poison or a slow; the opposite of a buff.
A stone every character carries that takes them back to the inn they last picked, with a long wait between uses.
Extra experience a character saves up while logged out in an inn or a capital city; it doubles the experience from monsters until it runs out.
Blizzard's game built on classic World of Warcraft, with new zones, quests and dungeons and no realm list; it opens Wed, Nov 4, 2026, 6 PM ET.
The name reservation window: pack holders can make up to three characters and keep their names, from Oct 27 until the end of Nov 3 Pacific (3 AM ET Nov 4).
The name of the group's voice channel on its Discord server.
What players usually did in World of Warcraft Classic, the older version of the game; a habit, not a Forever rule.
The level where one rank of a spell stops getting stronger; past it, only the next rank, learned from a trainer, hits harder.
